edges.description: Alpha-2C-AR activation is potentiated by RhoA/ROCK signaling.

The closest exposure-to-node fit in this tranche: the node is named for cold-induced vasoconstriction, and the first item names the receptor as the sole mediator of local cooling-induced vasoconstriction. Exposure and mechanism are in the same clause, which is why this one is direct where the others are not. Direct is recorded knowing that cold reaches the receptor through mitochondrial reactive oxygen species and RhoA/ROCK, which this entry models as a separate node: those steps sit inside the cold-induced vasoconstriction this node is named for rather than on the edge into it, so they are internal to the target and not intermediates the edge steps over. Noted so the question is not reopened later.

Pointed at sympathetic dysregulation rather than at the cold-receptor node, because that is the route this entry gives a stressor that is not cold, and the node's own description places increased sympathetic adrenergic control on the digital resistance vessels. The intermediates are recorded as known on the strength of that mapped route rather than of the quoted sentence, which stops at the vasospasm and does not name the nerves.

nodes.description: Cold triggers alpha-2C adrenoceptor (ADRA2C) activation in microvascular smooth muscle cells, mediating local cooling-induced vasoconstriction of digital arteries and arterioles. Alpha-2C-AR is the sole mediator of cold-induced vasoconstriction in the peripheral vasculature.

evidence.snippet: alterations in activity of the peripheral adrenoceptor have been implicated, specifically an enhanced smooth muscle contraction due to overexpression or hyperactivity of postsynaptic alpha 2 receptors

evidence.snippet: Raynaud's phenomenon (RP) is a condition characterized by episodic, excessive vasoconstriction in the fingers and toes, triggered by cold or stress.

nodes.description: Increased sympathetic adrenergic control of digital resistance vessels contributes to exaggerated cold-induced vasoconstriction. The pathogenesis involves a complex interaction between the vascular wall, nerves, hormones, and humoral factors disrupting the balance between vasoconstriction and vasodilation.
